Save a globe as an SVG file

Source: R/hex_globe.R
hex_globe_svg.Rd

Draws a globe from hex_globe as an SVG drawing, in the view the widget opens with: the ocean, the land, the cells and every line as vector paths, placed and projected as the widget's shader places them. The drawing is made on the CPU by the 'hexglobe' package and needs no graphics card or browser.

Usage

hex_globe_svg(widget, file, width = 800, height = 800, background = NULL)

Arguments

widget

A globe from hex_globe.

file

Path of the SVG file to write.

width, height

Size of the drawing in pixels.

background

Colour behind the globe, or NULL for none.

Value

file, invisibly.

Details

The cells of an ISEA grid, which the widget finds per pixel, are drawn as one path per colour and their borders as polylines, so the file grows with the number of cells drawn. Borders fade out where the cells shrink below a few pixels, as in the widget. Values blended across cells (smooth = TRUE) have no vector form and are refused; hex_globe_png draws them.

See also

hex_globe_png for the same view as a PNG image

Examples

if (requireNamespace("hexglobe", quietly = TRUE)) {
  grid <- hex_grid(resolution = 2, aperture = 3)
  globe <- hex_globe(grid, land = FALSE)
  hex_globe_svg(globe, tempfile(fileext = ".svg"), width = 300, height = 300)
}
